rover.name: Pressurised rover
rover.description: EVA start, end and radiation shelter. Parked on the south bank of Neretva Vallis, where Perseverance stopped on sols 1150–1154.
rover.science: Firm, elevated ground with a view over the channel. The crew walks from here; the rover does not enter the dune field.
rover.whyHumans: A crewed rover can reposition in minutes when the plan changes — no overnight command cycle from Earth.

cheyava.name: Cheyava Falls · Bright Angel
cheyava.description: Arrowhead-shaped rock, about 1 m × 0.6 m, on the northern edge of Neretva Vallis. White calcium-sulfate veins cut reddish mudstone dotted with pale 'leopard spots' ringed in dark minerals.
cheyava.science: Perseverance detected organic compounds here and cored the sample 'Sapphire Canyon' on sol 1215 (21 July 2024). In September 2025 NASA reported the spots as a potential biosignature — the strongest candidate found on Mars so far. It is not proof of life.
cheyava.whyHumans: A field geologist can split the rock along a vein, sample both sides of one reaction front, and pick the next target in minutes instead of sols.

serpentine.name: Serpentine Rapids
serpentine.description: Red outcrop on the south side of Neretva Vallis. Perseverance's abrasion patch exposed white, black and olive-green spots inside the rock (August 2024).
serpentine.science: The green spots resemble reduction spots in red rocks on Earth, where chemical reactions — sometimes involving microbes — strip iron of its colour. Comparing them with Cheyava Falls tests whether one process acted along the whole channel.
serpentine.whyHumans: Humans can trace a single layer across the outcrop by eye and hand, and collect a fresh, unweathered piece with a hammer.

washburn.name: Mount Washburn boulder field
washburn.description: Hill covered in boulders at the eastern end of the channel. One light-toned, speckled boulder, 'Atoko Point' (about 45 cm wide), is unlike other rocks seen in Jezero.
washburn.science: The boulders were carried here from elsewhere — possibly from deep in the crater rim. They are free samples of rocks the rover could not otherwise reach.
washburn.whyHumans: Sorting dozens of boulders by type takes a trained eye a few minutes; a rover needs days of imaging to do the same.

channel.name: Neretva Vallis floor
channel.description: Floor of the ancient river channel that once carried water into Jezero's lake. Perseverance drove along it on sols 1171–1175 to avoid a boulder field.
channel.science: Smooth, light bedrock exposed between dunes records the last water to flow through the valley.
channel.whyHumans: On foot the crew can cross dune gaps that would trap a wheeled rover.
